purpose: Teach the Film Studio product to generate recognizable metric-scale rigid-body archetypes whose visible fill state deterministically controls mass and center of mass, while Blender/Bullet retains exclusive authority over every post-release and final pose.

curriculumCorrection.retainedPc5Strength: procedural lathed bottle silhouette with readable base, body, shoulder, neck, cap and label
curriculumCorrection.retainedPc5Limitation: the accepted lesson used an approximately 0.84 m ball diameter, 1.44 m bottles and manually chosen identical target masses, so it did not establish metric physical archetypes
curriculumCorrection.retainedPc8Strength: evaluated Bullet motion selects the event and derives native shutter without final-pose authority
curriculumCorrection.pc9Change: return to three recognizable bottles at real-world scale and derive each rigid-body mass and object-origin center of mass from the same visible fill fraction

targets.centerOfMassFormula: mass-weighted container COM and visible liquid-column COM

machineAcceptance.schemaAndNegativeControls: all frozen v0.1-v0.4 controls plus new v0.5 mass, COM, profile, collision and authority attacks must pass before mutation

directVisualQuestions: At first glance, do the actor and all three targets read specifically as one basketball and three capped bottles rather than a sphere and generic blocks?
Do ball-to-bottle proportions look plausible at real-world metric scale?
Are three distinct liquid fill levels visible and consistent with the recorded low, medium and high fill inputs?
Does the contact sequence propagate continuously through Bullet rather than showing a simultaneous arranged lean or final-pose jump?
Does the measured blurred impact add speed while retaining ball seams, bottle silhouettes, caps, labels and contact direction?
Does the aftermath contain solver-discovered separation, support and differing angles rather than a neat placed composition?
Do material response, contact shadows and surface detail make the physical archetypes more credible than the PC8 abstract wooden targets?
visualVerdictRule: PASS only if all seven questions are YES on bound formal stills and the complete bound clip; photoreal film quality remains a separately reported claim ceiling

development.allowed: local product branch, repeated zero-network scene runs and screenshot review before product commit

stopRule: Retain and stop on any schema escape, derived mass/COM mismatch, initial penetration, missing target response, final-pose key, reopen mismatch, collision/visible-body mismatch, formal resource overrun or direct visual NO. Do not weaken thresholds or hand-place a better final image.
claimCeiling: A PASS establishes one product-integrated metric basketball/filled-bottle physical-archetype lesson. It does not establish liquid slosh simulation, deformation, photorealism, broad asset generalization or robot-capstone quality.
